physical: Going from a higher to a lower index, beyond the critical angle no light crosses the boundary; all of it is reflected, while an evanescent field reaches past the surface without carrying energy across. sin θ_c = n2 ÷ n1
reflected_formula: sin θ_c = n2 ÷ n1 (kept as given; θ_c and n have no frozen partners)
reflected_sentence: The formula keeps its form but the limit turns around: what read as a slant past which no light may cross now reads as a mark past which nothing is held back — the unreachable is already there, and what the gap returned now collects.
rule_reason: The cost 'crossing the boundary' rises with refractive index; judged to carry resistance here, making one resistance-cost, odd parity, so the reading turns while the formula stays.
interpretation: The banned word for the surface becomes the gap. A cost that rises with the medium's opposition flips to an ease that rises with receptivity. What was all returned now collects.
closing: Judgment call, the same one as the Fresnel row: refractive index is UNDETERMINED, and the turn depends entirely on reading the medium as resistance, which Ch 16's diffraction line supports and the ratio-of-speeds definition denies. I took the resistance reading because the statement's own cost rises with the index; on the other reading this row has zero costs of the relevant kind and would keep.
